Introduction

Starting a Home Care Agency in North Carolina enables you to provide non-medical personal care services. The NC Department of Health & Human Services — Division of Health Service Regulation oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand North Carolina’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand North Carolina’s Regulations

NC DHHS licenses home care agencies under state regulations. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the NC Secretary of State, apply for home care agency license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

NC benchmarks: Private pay rates $20-$28/hour, Medicaid rates $15-$22/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling systems, and documentation tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

NC requires background checks and training for all direct care staff.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting DHSR requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks across the Charlotte, Raleigh-Durham, and other metro areas.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality improvement programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
